Armor and damage types

The formulas below describe this engine's current rules. Item and spell examples are calculated from your loaded game data.

Why does this enemy resist my damage?

Check the damage types on your weapon or spell against the enemy's protection. High protection against fire does not protect against slashing. Equipment only helps where it covers the body, and broken armour provides no protection.

A worked example

For a single damage type, 30 incoming damage against 20 protection leaves 10. Against 40 protection, the original armour rule leaves zero; the 20% minimum rule leaves 6. The active rule is listed below.

For each damage type: remaining damage = max(minimum damage, incoming damage − natural armor − covering armor layers). Layers are applied from the outside inward. Different damage types do not absorb one another.

Active armor rule: Armor can absorb damage completely.

An item's protection for a damage type = coverage absorption × coverage type factor × material resistance. Primary and secondary coverage can differ. Broken equipment provides no protection.

Body partCovering equipment
HeadHelmet
TorsoPlate and shirt
ArmsPlate, shirt and gloves
LegsLeggings, pants and boots

Magic uses the armor for its actual damage type, which can differ from its knowledge school. Protection effects contribute the strongest matching protection. Lasting magic scales both damage and absorption per tick and distributes damage across body parts.
